name: DEBUG_LOG
description: Logs a label and numeric value to stdout for debugging. Returns the value unchanged.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: A label to identify the log entry

returns.description: The same value passed in (for chaining)

name: GET_FACTOR
signature: GET_FACTOR(key1, key2, key3, key4, key5, date)
description: Retrieves a factor value by up to 5 keys, effective on the given date

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The effective date to use for lookup

returns.description: The factor value for the specified keys on the given date

name: ROUND_CENTS
description: Rounds a monetary amount to cents using the specified rounding rule. Supports utility-specific rounding conventions.

returns.description: The rounded amount in cents (2 decimal places)

name: MAX
description: Returns the maximum of two values. Commonly used for minimum bill enforcement.

returns.description: The larger of the two values

name: MIN
description: Returns the minimum of two values. Useful for caps and limits.

returns.description: The smaller of the two values

name: GET_SEASON
description: Determines the billing season (SUMMER/WINTER) from the date and configurable summer month boundaries. Boundaries come from rate factors (not hardcoded), so winter-peaking utilities or any seasonal definition work. Handles wraparound ranges where summer_start > summer_end (e.g., a Nov-Mar summer).

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The billing date in YYYY-MM-DD format

parameters.name: summer_start
parameters.description: First month of summer (1-12), e.g., 6 for June

parameters.name: summer_end
parameters.description: Last month of summer (1-12), e.g., 9 for September

example:
summer_start = GET_FACTOR(INPUT.RATE, "SUMMER_START_MONTH", "", "", "", effective_date)
summer_end = GET_FACTOR(INPUT.RATE, "SUMMER_END_MONTH", "", "", "", effective_date)
season = GET_SEASON(INPUT.BILL_DATE, summer_start, summer_end)

name: EXTRACT_MONTH
description: Extracts the month number (1-12) from a date string.

name: CALCULATE_TIERED
description: Calculates energy charge using a two-tier rate structure. Usage up to tier1_limit is charged at tier1_rate, remainder at tier2_rate.

name: ABS
description: Returns the absolute value of a number. Useful for credit calculations.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to get absolute value of

name: ROUND
description: Rounds a number to the specified number of decimal places using standard rounding (half up)

parameters.name: decimals
parameters.description: Number of decimal places (e.g., 2 for cents)

name: ADD_YEARS
description: Adds the specified number of years to a date. Useful for date offset calculations.

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: Number of years to add (can be negative to subtract)

returns.description: The new date in YYYY-MM-DD format

name: ADD_MONTHS
description: Adds the specified number of months to a date. Handles year rollover automatically.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: Number of months to add (can be negative to subtract)

returns.description: The new date in YYYY-MM-DD format

name: CALCULATE_TIERED_N
description: Calculates charge using N-tier rate structure. Tiers are loaded from a factor as JSON array of {limit, rate} objects. Handles 1 to unlimited tiers.

parameters.name: tiers_json
parameters.description: JSON array of tier objects: [{"limit":500,"rate":0.05},{"limit":1000,"rate":0.08},{"limit":0,"rate":0.12}]. Last tier limit=0 means unlimited.

example:
tiers = GET_FACTOR(INPUT.RATE, "ENERGY_TIERS", "", "", "", INPUT.BILL_DATE)
energy_charge = CALCULATE_TIERED_N(INPUT.KWH, tiers)

name: GET_TOU_PERIOD
description: Determines the time-of-use period from a datetime and TOU schedule. Returns period name like ON_PEAK, OFF_PEAK, SHOULDER.

parameters.name: datetime
parameters.description: Datetime in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format or just HH:MM for hour extraction

returns.description: TOU period name (e.g., ON_PEAK, OFF_PEAK, SHOULDER)

example:
tou_schedule = GET_FACTOR(INPUT.RATE, "TOU_SCHEDULE", season, "", "", INPUT.BILL_DATE)
period = GET_TOU_PERIOD(INPUT.USAGE_HOUR, tou_schedule)

name: CLAMP
description: Constrains a value between a minimum and maximum. Used for rate caps, floors, and demand charge limits.

name: CALCULATE_RATCHET
description: Computes billing demand under a demand-ratchet clause: the greater of the current period's demand and a percentage of the highest demand over a trailing window. All prior peaks are passed in as a JSON array (stateless — the engine performs no historical lookups). Common for commercial/industrial tariffs outside Florida.

parameters.name: history_json
parameters.description: JSON array of prior-period peak demands, e.g. "[120.0, 135.5, 110.0]". Empty array means no ratchet floor applies.

parameters.name: ratchet_pct
parameters.description: Ratchet percentage as a decimal (e.g., 0.80 for an 80% ratchet)

name: POWER_FACTOR_ADJ
description: Applies a power-factor adjustment to a demand charge. When the customer's actual power factor is below the target, the demand charge is scaled up proportionally (target/actual); at or above target there is no penalty. Power factor is supplied at calculation time (stateless). Common in commercial/industrial tariffs.

parameters.name: demand_charge
parameters.description: The computed demand charge before adjustment

returns.description: Adjusted demand charge (increased when actual_pf < target_pf)

name: IS_EVENT_DAY
description: Returns 1.0 if the billing date is a declared critical-peak / event day, else 0.0. Event dates are passed in as a JSON array of YYYY-MM-DD strings (stateless — no event-calendar lookup). Used for Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) adders.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The date to test, in YYYY-MM-DD format

returns.description: 1.0 if date is an event day, 0.0 otherwise

name: GET_DAY_TYPE
description: Returns the day type (WEEKDAY or WEEKEND) for a date. Useful for TOU schedules that differ on weekends. Pure function of the date.
